card.title: User-defined bulk solvent map
card.summary: A small patch to phenix.refine lets users replace the default flat bulk-solvent mask with their own solvent map, for example one from molecular dynamics or 3D-RISM. On a 0.96 Å scorpion toxin test case, an MD-derived solvent map lowered Rfree from 0.147 to 0.109.

paper.title: Supplying a user-defined bulk solvent map for refinement

nodes.title: QUE - Where does the flat binary bulk-solvent mask fail to describe crystal solvent?
nodes.desc: Most refinement programs fill the region outside the atomic model with constant electron density. The paper lists the ways this assumption departs from real solvent.

nodes.title: QUE - Can phenix.refine use an externally computed bulk-solvent map in place of the flat mask?
nodes.desc: Physically richer solvent models exist, but Phenix had no way to take them as input. The paper asks whether a small local change can add this.

nodes.title: QUE - Does a user-supplied solvent map improve fit to the X-ray data compared with the flat mask?
nodes.desc: Fit is measured by R-work and cross-validated R-free on a high-resolution test structure.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement

nodes.title: QUE - How can a 48-member protein ensemble be refined and validated with a structured solvent model?
nodes.desc: The test case uses a large multiconformer ensemble, which strains standard validation tools.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement; Table 1

nodes.title: CLM - Inaccurate solvent modeling is a major driver of the gap between refinement R values and data quality
nodes.desc: Crystals are 20-90% solvent by volume, about 50% on average, and all of it scatters X-rays. Solvent is still modeled with crude approximations, which leaves a large R-factor gap.

nodes.title: CLM - A flat mask cannot represent structured density from waters, ions, lipids and buffer components
nodes.desc: The flat model assumes disordered solvent is spread evenly through the non-masked part of the asymmetric unit. Real solvent has structure that this ignores.

nodes.title: CLM - The binary mask treats the unoccupied fraction of partially occupied atoms as vacuum
nodes.desc: Any atom with occupancy below 1 is fully excluded from the solvent mask. This affects multiconformer models and partially occupied waters, and adding many low-occupancy waters to compensate inflates parameters and destabilizes refinement.

nodes.title: CLM - Sharp mask edges and solvent assigned to unmodeled regions leave systematic errors in difference maps
nodes.desc: Fourier ripples from the mask boundary appear at high resolution. Solvent density placed over unmodeled parts of the model smears density and lowers peak heights, which Polder maps can correct but refinement programs rarely use.

nodes.title: CLM - The mosaic bulk-solvent model improves on the flat mask but keeps the binary-boundary approximation
nodes.desc: The mosaic model gives each isolated solvent region its own occupancy. It still treats solvent as a structureless continuum and does not fix the partial-occupancy problem.

nodes.title: CLM - Physically based solvent models exist but have been hard to integrate into Phenix
nodes.desc: MD simulations, 3D-RISM, holographic methods such as EDEN and neural networks can all predict solvent density. Getting their output into standard refinement has been the practical barrier.
nodes.loc: Purpose; Background, paragraph 4; 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask', paragraph 1

nodes.title: CLM - Other refinement programs already accept a precomputed solvent or partial-structure contribution
nodes.desc: Buster, Refmac5, SHELXL, PLATON, AMBER and X-PLOR/CNS allow this. Refmac5 accepts up to five partial structures through FPART/PHIPART columns.
nodes.loc: 'The flat-mask bulk-solvent model is an approximation of structured solvent', paragraph 3

nodes.title: CLM - A compact local patch lets phenix.refine use user-supplied solvent structure factors as F_mask
nodes.desc: The user's amplitude and phase columns replace the flat-mask F_mask, and k_mask is still fit analytically per resolution bin, so the map can be on any scale. The map is held fixed during refinement and fully replaces the mask.
nodes.loc: 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask'; Scaling and treatment during refinement

nodes.title: CLM - Solvent MTZ files prepared for Refmac can be used in Phenix without relabeling
nodes.desc: The default column labels are FPART and PHIPART, following the Refmac convention. If the experimental MTZ already holds these columns, no separate file is needed.
nodes.loc: 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask', paragraph 2; Input specification

nodes.title: CLM - The supplied map must be carried through outlier rejection or it is silently discarded
nodes.desc: Each outlier-rejection step rebuilds the f_model manager. Without propagating the map through select(), Phenix recomputes the flat mask and the supplied map has no effect on the result.

nodes.title: CLM - The patch does not support joint X-ray/neutron refinement, and twin refinement is untested
nodes.desc: These are the two limitations the authors state for the current patch.
nodes.loc: 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask', paragraph 2

nodes.title: CLM - Replacing the flat mask with a physically based solvent map lowers cross-validated R-free
nodes.desc: For the 1AHO test case, both an MD-derived map in Phenix and 3D-RISM solvent in Table 1 gave lower R-free than flat bulk solvent.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement; Table 1

nodes.title: CLM - The R-free gain reflects a better solvent model rather than overfitting
nodes.desc: Free-flagged reflections were excluded from all map editing, so the R-free change is cross-validated. Model geometry did not change and the R-free/R-work gap stayed small.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement, paragraph 2

nodes.title: CLM - The size of the improvement will depend on resolution, solvent content and map quality
nodes.desc: The authors present 1AHO as a single test case, not a general benchmark. Its high-resolution, ambient-temperature data and nearly pure-water solvent make it a favorable system.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent, paragraph 1; text after Table 1

nodes.title: CLM - Ensemble modeling gave larger R-free gains than solvent map editing
nodes.desc: In the 1AHO series, density editing of the solvent map contributed small R-free gains compared with moving to a multiconformer ensemble.

nodes.title: CLM - Per-bin k_mask in Phenix corrects resolution-dependent miscalibration of MD solvent maps
nodes.desc: A single global B-factor applied to the MD map blurs it and suppresses its high-resolution content. Fitting k_mask per resolution bin restores that content, so fewer explicit waters are needed to patch the deficit.

nodes.title: CLM - Iterating refinement and solvent density editing further lowers R-free
nodes.desc: After refinement with the supplied map, remaining Fo-Fc features in the solvent are treated as missing structure and added back to the map. The README describes repeating this until solvent peaks fall below about 3 sigma.

nodes.title: CLM - Supercell ensembles refine as stably as single-ASU models and resolve non-bonded ambiguities
nodes.desc: The 48-member ensemble was refined as a 2x2x3 supercell with full-occupancy copies. It was condensed to one ASU with 48 altlocs only for this demonstration, because supercell refinement is not widely adopted.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement, paragraph 2

nodes.title: EVD - MD-derived map lowered R-free from 0.1473 to 0.1092 and R-work from 0.1278 to 0.0928
nodes.desc: Same starting ensemble, data and three macro-cycles in phenix.refine; only the solvent source differed. Part of the R-work gain is expected because the map was edited against working-set difference density.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement, results table

nodes.title: EVD - Bond r.m.s.d. was 0.007 Å in both the flat-mask and MD-map runs
nodes.desc: Model geometry was essentially unchanged by the switch in solvent source, and the R-free/R-work gap remained small.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement, paragraph 2

nodes.title: EVD - Flat bulk solvent gave R-free 0.1664; 3D-RISM solvent gave 0.1302
nodes.desc: Both runs used occupancy-refined waters. MolProbity scores were 2.94 for both.

nodes.title: EVD - map_touchup density editing lowered R-free only from 0.1181 to 0.1161
nodes.desc: This step followed the 48-copy supercell refinement with MD average solvent, ordered waters and watershed, which itself reached R-free 0.1181 from 0.1239 for the 2-8 conformer model.

nodes.title: EVD - msander plus Refmac5 supercell refinement reached R-free 0.1107 with MolProbity 1.06
nodes.desc: The single-ASU phenix.refine run with 48 altlocs reached R-free 0.1089, but MolProbity crashed on it.

nodes.title: EVD - Flat-mask k_mask was 0.00 above 3 Å; MD-map k_mask was 1.12 to 1.45 there
nodes.desc: At low resolution (14-6.7 Å) k_mask was 0.33 for the flat mask and 1.05 for the MD map. Values above 1 at high resolution indicate the global B-factor had undersold the map amplitude.

nodes.title: EVD - Iterated density editing reached R-work 0.084 and R-free 0.105
nodes.desc: Compared with 0.093 and 0.109 after the first cycle with the ensemble Fpart/PHIpart map, and 0.128 and 0.147 with the flat mask.

nodes.title: EVD - Without propagation through select(), k_mask was fit to a recomputed flat mask
nodes.desc: Outlier removal rebuilt the f_model manager, which dropped the stored map, so the supplied map had no effect until the patch carried it through the in-place selection path.
nodes.loc: Reflection outlier rejection; README: Implementation notes

nodes.title: EVD - The patch changes three files: +23, +46 and +25/-12 lines
nodes.desc: A new PHIL scope in __init__.params, an injection helper in phenix_refine.py, and set_user_f_masks() plus propagation in f_model.py.
nodes.loc: Modified source files table; README: Files changed

nodes.title: STU - phenix.refine of 1AHO with the default flat mask versus an MD-derived solvent map
nodes.desc: Scorpion toxin II at 0.96 Å, 29,557 reflections over 0.96-15.8 Å with 1,444 (5%) in the free set. Two otherwise identical protocols from the repository.

nodes.title: STU - Series of solvent and ensemble models refined against 1AHO data (Table 1)
nodes.desc: Refmac5, 3D-RISM, MD-average solvent, supercell, density editing and msander refinements compared by R-work, R-free and MolProbity score.

nodes.title: STU - Per-resolution-bin k_mask comparison of flat mask and MD map
nodes.desc: k_mask values from phenix.refine for each resolution bin, with the flat mask and with the MD-derived Fpart map.

nodes.title: STU - Iterated refinement and density editing of the 1AHO solvent map
nodes.desc: Repeated cycles of refinement with the supplied map, Fo-Fc inspection and density editing.

nodes.title: STU - Development and debugging of the patch against prior Refmac5 results
nodes.desc: The feature was added to a nightly Phenix build with an AI coding agent, using earlier Refmac5 results as the validation target. Several debugging rounds isolated the minimal set of edits.
nodes.loc: LLM Disclosure Statement; Reflection outlier rejection

nodes.title: PRO - Apply the three phenix_user_solvent patches to a Phenix installation
nodes.desc: Patch f_model.py, phenix/programs/phenix_refine.py and __init__.params under site-packages (Phenix 2.x) or modules/ (Phenix 1.21 and earlier). Other files named phenix_refine.py must not be patched.

nodes.title: PRO - phenix.refine with refinement.input.bulk_solvent_map
nodes.desc: Pass file_name, amplitudes_label and phases_label. The 1AHO runs used three macro-cycles refining individual sites and ADPs.
nodes.loc: Input specification; Map ingestion and indexing; Effect on refinement

nodes.title: PRO - MD-derived solvent map with density editing
nodes.desc: Average solvent density from an AMBER trajectory with crystal packing, then add Fo-Fc difference features back into the map with free-flagged reflections excluded. The ensemble was optimized with msander, ramping the X-ray term while lowering temperature.

nodes.title: PRO - Iterative refine, inspect and density-edit cycle
nodes.desc: Refine with the user map for 3-10 cycles, export FMASK and K_MASK, add positive solvent blobs to the solvent MTZ and repeat. Stop when the k_mask profile stabilizes and solvent Fo-Fc peaks fall below about 3 sigma.

nodes.title: PRO - 48-copy supercell ensemble refinement
nodes.desc: Data and solvent structure factors re-indexed by 2h,2k,3l, the cell enlarged 2x2x3 in P212121, and filled with 48 full-occupancy copies of the monomer.
nodes.loc: Example of AMBER bulk solvent: Effect on refinement, paragraph 2

nodes.title: REQ - Benchmark user-supplied solvent maps on a larger set of structures
nodes.desc: The authors state that future analysis will test the approach beyond the single 1AHO case.

nodes.title: REQ - Adopt the bulk-solvent map feature in Phenix itself
nodes.desc: The patch is intended as a feature request to the Phenix developers.

nodes.title: REQ - Support joint X-ray/neutron refinement and test twin refinement with a supplied map
nodes.desc: Listed as the current limitations of the patch.
nodes.loc: 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask', paragraph 2; README: Known limitations

nodes.title: REQ - Neural network prediction of solvent density from protein structure alone
nodes.desc: Named as a future method whose output map could be Fourier-transformed and supplied in the same way (cowcat repository).
nodes.loc: 'A user-supplied bulk solvent map can replace the flat mask', paragraph 1
